Title: Bahi-Khata: Papa ka Pehla Bill
Problem it solves: Haath ke bahi-khata se billing: rush mein lambi line, thakaan mein galat total, aur kis batch ki dawa kisko gayi, kab expire hogi, iska koi record nahi.
Audience: Family-run medical stores in north Indian towns still billing by hand (bahi, bill book, calculator); owners 45-70 and their tech-savvy sons/daughters 22-35; Hindi-speaking.

Title: Chaar goli, chauntees rupaye?!
Problem it solves: Patte se khuli goli bechte waqt counter staff per-goli daam galat jodta hai, har baar alag rate banta hai aur customer se bahas hoti hai.
Audience: Medical store owners and pharmacists in India (25-60) who sell loose tablets from strips and rely on staff doing mental maths or a calculator at the counter

Title: Das Minute: Inspector Aa Rahe Hain
Problem it solves: Drug inspector achanak aate hain, aur rush ke dino mein haath ka Schedule H1 register adhoora reh jaata hai: kaunsi H1 dawa, kis mareez ko, kis doctor ki parchi pe.
Audience: Medical store owners, licence holders and pharmacists in Indian towns (30-60) who still keep Schedule H/H1 registers by hand and worry about inspections; Hindi-speaking.

Title: Jo Dawa Kabhi Biki Hi Nahi
Problem it solves: Expired stock ka nuksaan chupchaap hota hai: kaunsa batch kab expire hoga kisi ko yaad nahi rehta, aur dawa bikne se pehle hi bekaar ho jaati hai.
Audience: Medical store owners and pharmacists (25-55) in Indian towns and cities with large shelf stock and regular near-expiry write-offs; single stores and small chains; Hindi-speaking.

Title: Breaking News: Sharma ji ki Neend aur GST 5%
Problem it solves: 22 Sep 2025 se zyaadatar dawaon pe GST 5% hai; rate badalne ke baad dukaandaar ko darr rehta hai ki return mein HSN chhoot gaya ya lautayi dawa ka credit note galat gaya, aur galti filing ke baad hi pakdi jaayegi.
Audience: GST-registered medical store owners (30-60) and the family member or accountant who files their GSTR-1/3B; small towns and cities of north India; Hindi-speaking; interest in GST, pharmacy business, accounting.

Title: Shaam 7 Baje: Pehle vs Ab
Problem it solves: Shaam ke rush mein 'dawa hai ya nahi' dekhne ke liye rack khangaalna aur calculator pe total lagana billing slow karta hai; line lambi hoti hai aur grahak bina dawa liye laut jaata hai.
Audience: Busy medical store owners and counter staff in towns and cities with an evening rush; 22-55; Hindi-speaking north India.

Title: Bill ki naav ban gayi!
Problem it solves: Customer ka kaagaz ka bill kho gaya jo office reimbursement claim ke liye chahiye; dukaan ko bill-book palatne aur duplicate chhaapne mein waqt aur kaagaz dono barbaad hote hain.
Audience: Medical store owners and pharmacists in India who still use carbon bill books or reprint duplicate bills, and want to send bills on WhatsApp; ages 25-55

Title: Ek Password Ka Raaz
Problem it solves: Sab staff ek hi login se bill banate hain: discount badhta hai, stock ghatta hai, aur owner bata nahi sakta ki kisne kya badla, to shak sab par jaata hai.
Audience: Medical store owners (32-60) with 2-6 counter staff, and their sons/daughters who run the shop software; worried about unexplained discounts and stock mismatch; Hindi-speaking north and central India.

Title: Hisaab Machine Ka, Waqt Pari Ka
Problem it solves: Din band karne ka cash aur hisaab haath se milane mein ghante lagte hain; dukaan wala raat der tak counter pe atka rehta hai aur parivaar ke khaas pal chhoot jaate hain.
Audience: Medical store owners (35-55) with families, running the counter themselves and closing cash and accounts by hand every night; north Indian towns; Hindi-speaking; also their spouses who co-run the shop.

Title: Chaar Panne ka Bill: Purchase Entry, Samjhaayi Gayi
Problem it solves: Distributor ke lambe bill ki har line (batch, expiry, MRP, rate) haath se type karne mein ghante lagte hain, aur 10+1 jaisi scheme ka free maal galat chadh jaaye to har item ki cost aur bechne ka rate galat ho jaata hai.
Audience: Medical store owners, pharmacists and staff who enter distributor purchase bills (weekly 20-100 line bills, scheme/free goods); small towns and cities of north India; Hindi-speaking; 22-55.

Title: Quiz: Ek Strip Ki Asli Cost Kitni?
Problem it solves: Scheme (free maal) aur discount ke baad ek strip ya bottle ki asli cost malik ko yaad nahi rehti, isliye thok ya regular grahak ko galat rate bol dete hain: zyada bolo to grahak jaata hai, kam bolo to munafa.
Audience: Medical store owners and pharmacists who buy on distributor schemes and give bulk or regular-customer rates; 25-60; Hindi-speaking north India.

Title: Baarish ki woh raat
Problem it solves: Roz bikne wali dawai ka stock chupchaap khatam ho gaya kyunki order yaad ke bharose hota tha; raat ko ek maa ko khaali haath lautna pada aur dukaan ka bharosa toota.
Audience: Medical store owners and pharmacists in India (28-60) who track stock by memory or a notebook and lose customers to stock-outs of fast-moving medicines

Title: Kal De Dunga!
Problem it solves: Udhaar ek copy mein likha jaata hai: 340 aur 840 ek jaise dikhte hain, purani baaki bhool jaati hai, aur purane grahak se paise maangna ajeeb lagta hai.
Audience: Neighbourhood medical store owners in small towns (35-65) who give udhaar to regular customers and track it in a notebook; Hindi-speaking north India.

Title: Dhanteras Rush: Sabka Bill, Saath-Saath
Problem it solves: Diwali/festival ki shaam ek saath bahut saare grahak counter pe aa jaate hain; ek bill atakta hai toh poori line ruk jaati hai aur grahak naraz hote hain.
Audience: Busy medical stores in markets and colonies that see festival-evening rushes (Dhanteras, Diwali, Chhath, Eid); owners 28-55 and counter staff; Hindi-speaking; Meta Reels and YouTube in the festive season.

Title: Ek Counter Se: Chhoti Dukaan ka Software
Problem it solves: Chhoti medical store ko lagta raha ki achha pharmacy software ya toh bahut mehenga hai ya itna mushkil ki chalaya hi na jaaye; isliye dukaan bahi, calculator aur yaaddaasht ke bharose chalti rahi.
Audience: Small and family-run medical stores across India (single counter, 1-4 staff) that have not adopted software because of cost or complexity; owners 30-65 and their family; Hindi-speaking; retarget viewers of the earlier campaign films.
